newsitem.title: JORDAN: EU team checks barriers to Jordan economic reform.
newsitem.headline: EU team checks barriers to Jordan economic reform.

text.p: A European delegation reviewing progress in Jordan's economic reforms said on Wednesday it was looking into "bottlenecks" holding up major overhauls such as privatisation and legislative changes.

Harold Cool, European Commission desk officer for Jordan, said the team was assessing implementation of commitments to privatisation, legal and financial sector reforms and introduction of a social "safety net" to recompense those hardest hit by economic transition.

He said the team's report could affect the timing of a second bloc of European grants to Jordan worth 40 million Ecus ($46 million), agreed last September and aimed at easing pressure on Jordan's precarious balance of payments.
"The mandate of our mission is to assess the compliance with the second tranche conditions," Cool told a news conference.
"Our overall view is positive. In that sense we want to praise the Jordanian authorities for their continued commitment to their economic reform programme," he said.
